name: PEDIATRIC High-Risk Neuroblastoma (COG multiphase: multiagent induction, high-dose consolidation with autologous stem cell rescue, anti-GD2 dinutuximab + sargramostim post-consolidation, isotretinoin maintenance)
histology: neuroblastoma (peripheral neuroblastic tumor); high-risk group assignment is driven by stage, age, MYCN status, histology (INPC), ploidy, and segmental chromosomal aberrations
stage: high-risk (INRG; MYCN amplification assigns high-risk except completely resected INRG L1)

biomarkers.MYCN: amplification (risk-defining; MYCN amplification assigns the high-risk group rather than low/intermediate risk)
biomarkers.note: PEDIATRIC. MYCN amplification is the key risk-defining biomarker: detection of MYCN amplification in tumor cells assigns the high-risk group (except completely resected INRG Stage L1 disease). ALK, DNA ploidy, histology (INPC favorable/unfavorable), and segmental chromosomal aberrations (SCAs) also contribute to risk classification. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroblastoma v2.2026, INRG Risk Classification (line 278), Principles of Systemic Therapy (MYCN status, lines 1216, 1266 to 1269) and Molecular/Genetic Characterization (line 935). No endorsement implied.

treatmentSetting: consolidation (high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell rescue)
lineOfTherapy: first-line, newly diagnosed high-risk neuroblastoma (multiphase curative-intent therapy)

eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Overview of Treatment for High-Risk Neuroblastoma (line 587); Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease (line 1366 to 1394)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: induction to best response, then consolidation with high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem cell rescue for PR or better, then post-consolidation anti-GD2 immunotherapy and isotretinoin
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Principles of Systemic Therapy (induction line 1373 to 1394; consolidation line 1646; post-consolidation line 1682); end-induction reassessment (line 1430 to 1443)

drugs.name: Topotecan

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Chemotherapy Induction Regimens (NEUROB-D 7 of 13): Topotecan 1.2 mg/m2/dose Days 1 to 5 (line 1591)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC induction (21-day cycles). Topotecan is given with cyclophosphamide as cycles 1 and 2 of the ANBL0532-derived induction backbone (Discussion lines 1385 to 1387; regimen line 1591). Dose banding for young children/lower BSAs applies (footnote d, line 1609).

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Chemotherapy Induction Regimens (NEUROB-D 7 of 13): Cyclophosphamide 400 mg/m2/dose Days 1 to 5 (line 1592)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC induction cycles 1 to 2 (topotecan/cyclophosphamide pair). Mesna may be used with cycles 1 and 2 as clinically indicated (footnote f, line 1612).

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Chemotherapy Induction Regimens (NEUROB-D 7 of 13): Cisplatin 50 mg/m2/dose Days 1 to 4, cycles 3 and 5 (lines 1593, 1598)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC induction cycles 3 and 5 (cisplatin/etoposide). ISMP tall-man (CISplatin). Cisplatin ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity carry higher stakes in children (language development at risk): mandatory pre/post hydration with electrolyte repletion and serial audiometry when the dose is administered.

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Chemotherapy Induction Regimens (NEUROB-D 7 of 13): Etoposide 200 mg/m2/dose Days 1 to 3, cycles 3 and 5 (lines 1594, 1599)

drugs.name: vinCRIStine

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Chemotherapy Induction Regimens (NEUROB-D 7 of 13): Vincristine (age-, weight-, and BSA-based dosing) Days 1 to 3, cycle 4 (line 1595)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC induction cycle 4 (vincristine/doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide). The source prints vincristine as age-, weight-, and BSA-based dosing and does NOT print a milligram value, so basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are the literal VERIFY (never invented). ISMP tall-man (vinCRIStine); 2 mg per-dose cap retained as a standard safety guard.

drugs.name: DOXOrubicin

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Chemotherapy Induction Regimens (NEUROB-D 7 of 13): Doxorubicin 25 mg/m2/dose Days 1 to 3, cycle 4 (line 1596)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC induction cycle 4. ISMP tall-man (DOXOrubicin). Pediatric anthracycline cumulative ceilings are LOWER than the adult 450/550 mg/m2 thresholds; a specific pediatric lifetime cap is not printed in this source, so a conservative pediatric cumulativeLifetime guard (warn 250 / hard 350 mg/m2, below the adult 450/550) is applied pending an institutional pediatric cap. Dexrazoxane may be used as clinically indicated (footnote f, line 1612); track cumulative anthracycline exposure and monitor LVEF.

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Chemotherapy Induction Regimens (NEUROB-D 7 of 13): Cyclophosphamide 2100 mg/m2/dose Days 1 to 2, cycle 4 (line 1597)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC induction cycle 4 (higher-dose cyclophosphamide with vincristine/doxorubicin). Mesna MUST be used with cycle 4 (footnote f, line 1612).

drugs.name: Dinutuximab (anti-GD2)

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Post-Consolidation Therapy (NEUROB-D 9 of 13): Dinutuximab 17.5 mg/m2/dose IV Days 4 to 7, 28-day cycles (line 1686)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC POST-CONSOLIDATION phase (Isotretinoin/Sargramostim + Dinutuximab), 28-day cycles for 6 cycles (footnote j, line 1705). Anti-GD2 antibody: severe neuropathic pain (requires scheduled opioid analgesia and pre-medication), capillary leak/hypotension, and cytokine-release/infusion reactions are expected class toxicities requiring monitored administration.

drugs.name: Sargramostim (GM-CSF)

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Post-Consolidation Therapy (NEUROB-D 9 of 13): Sargramostim 250 micrograms/m2/dose SQ Days 1 to 14, 28-day cycles (line 1685)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC POST-CONSOLIDATION phase (28-day cycles). Source prints Sargramostim 250 micrograms/m2/dose SQ Days 1 to 14; 250 micrograms/m2 equals 0.25 mg/m2 (exact unit conversion because the schema unit enum has no micrograms/m2 branch, not an invented value). GM-CSF potentiates the anti-GD2 antibody effect.

drugs.name: Isotretinoin (13-cis-retinoic acid)

provenance.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, High-Risk Disease: Post-Consolidation Therapy (NEUROB-D 9 of 13): Isotretinoin 80 mg/m2/dose PO twice daily Days 11 to 24, 28-day cycles (line 1687)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC maintenance/differentiation therapy (80 mg/m2/dose PO TWICE DAILY on Days 11 to 24 of each 28-day cycle). Isotretinoin is a potent TERATOGEN: strict pregnancy prevention and counseling are mandatory for patients of childbearing potential; monitor mucocutaneous toxicity, triglycerides, and hepatic function.

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration
premedications.notes: intravenous pre- and post-hydration with magnesium/potassium repletion before cisplatin (induction cycles 3 and 5)

premedications.name: Mesna
premedications.notes: MUST accompany cyclophosphamide in cycle 4; may accompany cycles 1 and 2 as clinically indicated (footnote f, line 1612)

premedications.name: Anti-GD2 pre-medication
premedications.notes: analgesia (scheduled opioid), antihistamine, antipyretic, and hydration before each dinutuximab infusion for neuropathic pain and capillary-leak/CRS control

supportiveCare: cycleLengthDays 21 and cycles 5 describe the INDUCTION backbone (all induction cycles are 21-day; a 5-cycle induction per ANBL12P1/ANBL1531 is recommended, Discussion lines 1388 to 1394). The dinutuximab, sargramostim, and isotretinoin entries belong to the 28-day post-consolidation/maintenance phase (6 cycles, footnote j line 1705) that follows consolidation, not to the 21-day induction cadence.

CONSOLIDATION phase (between induction and post-consolidation, not modeled as regimen drugs): high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell rescue. Single Transplant Option 1 (carboplatin weight/BSA/GFR-based Days -7 to -4; Etoposide 338 mg/m2/dose Days -7 to -4; Melphalan 70 mg/m2/dose Days -7 to -5) or Option 2 (busulfan age/weight-based Days -6 to -3; Melphalan 140 mg/m2/dose Day -1) or Tandem Transplant (Thiotepa 300 mg/m2/dose Days -7 to -5 + Cyclophosphamide 1500 mg/m2/dose Days -5 to -2, then a CEM course) per NEUROB-D 8 of 13 (lines 1646 to 1658). Carboplatin dose is weight-, BSA-, and GFR-based (VERIFY per protocol).
cisplatin: pre/post hydration, magnesium/potassium repletion, and serial audiometry (oto/nephrotoxicity stakes are higher in children).
doxorubicin: pediatric anthracycline ceilings are lower than adult; dexrazoxane may be used; track cumulative dose and LVEF.
dinutuximab: neuropathic pain (scheduled opioids), capillary-leak/hypotension, and cytokine-release/infusion reactions require monitored administration.
isotretinoin: teratogenicity - mandatory pregnancy prevention/counseling for patients of childbearing potential.
G-CSF: induction is myelosuppressive; add per febrile-neutropenia risk.
IL-2/aldesleukin is NOT part of the current NCCN-printed post-consolidation regimen (Isotretinoin/Sargramostim + Dinutuximab), so it is intentionally omitted rather than invented.

monitoring: disease reassessment at end of induction (critical decision point; PR or better proceeds to consolidation) (lines 1430 to 1443)
renal function (creatinine/GFR) and audiometry before/around cisplatin and carboplatin
cumulative anthracycline dose tracking (DOXOrubicin) and LVEF
anti-GD2 infusion monitoring: pain, blood pressure/capillary leak, cytokine-release reactions (dinutuximab)
isotretinoin: pregnancy testing/prevention, triglycerides, liver function, mucocutaneous toxicity
audiograms/brainstem auditory evoked response given critical age for language development (footnote k, line 1706)

doseModificationRules.condition: less than PR at end of induction
doseModificationRules.text: End-induction response below PR requires individualized decision-making; bridging chemoimmunotherapy (anti-GD2 + irinotecan/temozolomide/sargramostim) may be appropriate before or instead of consolidation; clinical review required (lines 1438 to 1445).
Hold or reduce per labeling and clinical review; ensure hydration, electrolyte repletion, and audiometry (higher stakes in children).

doseModificationRules.condition: severe anti-GD2 neuropathic pain, capillary leak, or cytokine-release
doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt or slow infusion, escalate analgesia and supportive care per labeling and clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Neuroblastoma is covered as an adult-text pediatric tumor; per-drug pediatric induction/immunotherapy milligram doses are not printed in the provided adult extract, so identity and doses are grounded to the NCCN Neuroblastoma guideline layer

guideline.locator: Overview of Treatment for High-Risk Neuroblastoma (line 587); Principles of Systemic Therapy: Induction (line 1373), Chemotherapy Induction Regimens NEUROB-D 7 of 13 (lines 1587 to 1609), High-Dose Consolidation Regimens NEUROB-D 8 of 13 (lines 1646 to 1658), Post-Consolidation Therapy NEUROB-D 9 of 13 (lines 1682 to 1689); MYCN risk assignment (lines 278, 1216, 1266 to 1269)

provenanceNote: PEDIATRIC ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for high-risk neuroblastoma (StewardMD reference disease neuroblastoma), modeled as the COG multiphase pathway: multiagent induction, high-dose consolidation with autologous stem cell rescue, post-consolidation anti-GD2 immunotherapy (dinutuximab + sargramostim), and isotretinoin maintenance. Regimen identity, phase sequence, and the risk-defining MYCN-amplification biomarker are grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroblastoma v2.2026 (Overview line 587; Principles of Systemic Therapy lines 1366 to 1445; MYCN risk assignment lines 278, 1216, 1266 to 1269). Induction milligram doses ARE printed for this age group and are captured verbatim by locator: Topotecan 1.2 mg/m2 D1 to 5 (line 1591), Cyclophosphamide 400 mg/m2 D1 to 5 cycles 1 to 2 (line 1592) and 2100 mg/m2 D1 to 2 cycle 4 (line 1597), Cisplatin 50 mg/m2 D1 to 4 cycles 3 and 5 (lines 1593, 1598), Etoposide 200 mg/m2 D1 to 3 cycles 3 and 5 (lines 1594, 1599), Doxorubicin 25 mg/m2 D1 to 3 cycle 4 (line 1596). Vincristine is printed only as age-, weight-, and BSA-based dosing (line 1595), so its basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are the literal VERIFY and are listed in verifyFields rather than invented. Post-consolidation doses are printed and captured: Dinutuximab 17.5 mg/m2 IV D4 to 7 (line 1686), Sargramostim 250 micrograms/m2 (0.25 mg/m2, exact unit conversion) SQ D1 to 14 (line 1685), Isotretinoin 80 mg/m2 PO twice daily D11 to 24 (line 1687), all on 28-day cycles (footnote j, line 1705). The consolidation high-dose conditioning options (CEM single, busulfan/melphalan, or thiotepa/cyclophosphamide tandem; lines 1646 to 1658) are documented in supportiveCare rather than modeled as 21-day induction drugs; the induction cycleLengthDays 21 and cycles 5 apply to the induction backbone only. Pediatric-specific safety is retained: cisplatin oto/nephrotoxicity monitoring with audiometry (higher stakes in children), anthracycline cumulativeLifetime set to a conservative pediatric guard (warn 250 / hard 350 mg/m2, below the adult 450/550; institutional pediatric cap to be confirmed) (dexrazoxane per footnote f, line 1612), dinutuximab neuropathic-pain/capillary-leak/CRS control, and isotretinoin teratogenicity precautions. IL-2/aldesleukin is intentionally omitted because it is not in the current NCCN-printed post-consolidation regimen. ISMP tall-man applied (vinCRIStine 2 mg cap, DOXOrubicin, CISplatin). Status is DRAFT with one unresolved VERIFY drug (vincristine). This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
